meta.title: Computer Upgrades for DOLE Main, 2002
meta.description: A contracting process with an award but NO recorded contract. The flagship example of data gaps: OCDS's structured record makes the missing contract visible (a dangling award with no contracts[] referencing it), where a flat export hides the gap entirely. Represents the ~19% of PhilGEPS processes with awards but no contract in the export.
meta.shapeNote: Shaped on real PhilGEPS record ocds-philgeps-1470-department-of-labor-and-employment-main. The real record DOES have a contract; this example deliberately omits it to represent the ~19% award-only bucket (measured in ocds/sample/compiled_releases.jsonl) and to teach how gaps appear in OCDS. See gapAnalysis below.

event.buyer: Department of Labor and Employment - Main
event.story: DOLE posts a small-value notice for computer upgrades via Shopping. A supplier is selected and the award is made — but the contract record is never captured in the export. The process is 'complete' as far as the tender and award go, but the lifecycle is partial from the data's point of view.

redFlags.name: Award without contract
redFlags.explanation: An award exists (awards[0].id = '1470', status 'active') but no contract links back to it — contracts[] is ABSENT, not empty. Either the contract wasn't captured, or it was never formalized. This is the case for ~19% of PhilGEPS processes. See gapAnalysis below for what this gap blocks.

steps.note: ONE source datum populated THREE OCDS identifier fields across two releases. Confusing them is the classic bug.
Published in release 002. The award exists.

DANGLING — no contract references this awardID. This is the gap made visible. A flat export would just show an empty Contract Amount cell; OCDS shows an unreferenced award object, which machines and humans can detect.
The gap itself becomes a signal. Future contract-value indicators (e.g. final price vs award value) cannot run — see gapAnalysis.blockedIndicators.

gapAnalysis._purpose: The teaching payload of this example. OCDS's structured record makes data gaps visible in a way flat exports hide. This section enumerates what's missing, how it shows up in the record, and what it blocks downstream.

flatExportView.whatYouSee: A row with Award No. = 1470, Award Amount = 107850, and a blank Contract Amount cell.
flatExportView.whyItHidesTheGap: A blank cell is ambiguous — it could mean 'not yet awarded', 'contract not captured', 'no contract required', or 'data entry skipped'. There's no structural signal that an award was made but never linked to a contract. The gap is invisible unless you already know to ask.

ocdsView.whatYouSee: awards[0] exists with id='1470', status='active', value=107850. contracts[] is ABSENT (not an empty array — the key is missing).
ocdsView.whyItShowsTheGap: The award object is a first-class citizen with a stable id. Any contract that formalises this award MUST reference it via contracts[].awardID = '1470'. The absence of any such reference is a machine-detectable signal: an 'active' award with no implementing contract. A validator (libcoveocds) or a simple jq query can find every dangling award in a dataset — impossible in a flat export.
ocdsView.queryToFindIt: jq 'select(.awards | length > 0) | select((.contracts // []) | map(.awardID) | index(.awards[0].id) | not)' compiled_releases.jsonl

blockedIndicators.name: Final contract value vs award value
blockedIndicators.whyItMatters: A common integrity check: does the final price exceed the award price? Cannot run without the contract value. In real data this is one of the most basic price-integrity signals, and it's blocked for ~19% of PhilGEPS processes.

blockedIndicators.name: Time from award to contract signing
blockedIndicators.whyItMatters: Long gaps between award and contract can signal procedural issues. Cannot compute without the contract date.

blockedIndicators.name: Delivery / transaction tracking
blockedIndicators.whyItMatters: Whether goods were actually delivered and paid for. Entirely opaque in this record.

gapAnalysis.teachingNote: This is the core argument for OCDS over flat exports: structure turns ambiguity into signal. A blank cell in a spreadsheet says nothing; a missing contracts[] with an active awards[0] says 'this award was never formalised, and here is exactly which award'. The primer's Analyzed station should let the learner toggle this gap on/off and watch the blocked indicators appear/disable in real time.
